_comment: Phase 3.6 release gates. Thresholds live here rather than in code so raising or lowering a bar is a reviewable diff with a reason attached. Run: poetry run python -m app.utils.release_gate

reliability._min_tasks_why: Below this the window says nothing. A gate that passes because no tasks ran would wave through a broken system, so it reports SKIPPED instead of PASS.
reliability._max_failure_rate_why: Roadmap 30-day target. Measured 5.7% over 7d before Phase 0/1 landed; 4% is the next step down, not the end state (90-day target is 2%).
reliability._max_turn_limit_why: Phase 0 converts turn exhaustion into continuations, so ANY turn-limit failure is a regression of that mechanism rather than a tuning issue.
reliability._max_provider_why: Zero since 2026-09-01. This gate holds that line.
reliability._max_cost_why: Guards against continuations silently multiplying spend. Generous on purpose: it is a runaway detector, not a budget.

telemetry._why: Phase 1 found the dashboard reporting 0 errors while 41 tasks had failed. That class of bug makes every other gate meaningless, because the system would be optimising against false health.

retrieval._why: Phase 3.1 baseline with collapse is recall 0.975 / MRR 0.963 / 0 misses. Floors sit below that because the embedding model is pinned by name, not hash, so a model update may move scores slightly.
